parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the image formed by a converging lens. Refer to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) • Switch on the lamp. • Place the screen a distance D = 80.0 cm from the illuminated object (the triangular hole in the card). • Place the lens close to the illuminated object. • Move the lens away from the illuminated object until a magnified, sharp image of the illuminated object is formed on the screen. • Do not move the illuminated object, the lens or the screen after this image position is found. Measure, to the nearest 0.1 cm, the object distance x 1 from the centre of the lens to the illuminated object. x 1 = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text: x recorded to the nearest millimetre

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Continue to move the lens away from the illuminated object until a diminished, sharp image of the illuminated object is formed on the screen. Measure, to the nearest 0.1 cm, the object distance y 1 from the centre of the lens to the illuminated object. y 1 = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The focal length f of the lens can be found using the equation: f = (D 2 – d 2 ) 4D . Use the value of D from (a)(i) and d from (a)(iii) to calculate a value f 1 for the focal length of the lens. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. f 1 = ................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
f1 calculation correct
answer given to 2 or 3 significant figures

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a second value f 2 for the focal length of the lens using the equation in (b) and your values in (c)(i). f 2 = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Two quantities can be considered to be equal within the limits of experimental accuracy if their values are within 10% of each other. State whether your values of f 1 and f 2 from (b) and (c)(ii) can be considered equal. Support your statement with a calculation. statement .................................................................................................................................. ................................................................................................................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
statement to match results
values used in a calculation to justify the statement

ms.text: move the lens slowly / backwards and forwards
